quote: Use a balloon to indicate when users attempt to exceed the maximum input size.
rule: In a password or PIN field, say when typing would exceed the maximum length.

section: Guidelines > Password and PIN text boxes
quote: To prevent information disclosure, the balloon should mention only documented facts about valid passwords or PINs.
rule: When a password or PIN field rejects a character, say so using only the documented rules, and prefer having no character restrictions at all.

quote: Consider using a balloon to indicate when users attempt to exceed the maximum input size for critical, short text boxes aimed at novice users.
rule: In short, important fields for novices, such as user names, say when typing would exceed the maximum length rather than only beeping.

quote: When users click a balloon, just dismiss the balloon without displaying any other UI or having any other side effect.
rule: Clicking a field message only dismisses it, with no other effect, and it has no close button.

quote: Choose the icon based on the usage pattern:
rule: An input problem message has no error symbol; a special-condition message has the warning symbol.

quote: Use title text that briefly summarizes the input problem or special condition in clear, plain, concise, specific language.
rule: The message's title sums up the problem or condition briefly in plain, specific words.

quote: Use text fragments or complete sentences without ending punctuation.
rule: The title is a fragment or sentence with no ending punctuation.

quote: Use sentence-style capitalization.
rule: The title is in sentence case.

quote: Use no more than 48 characters (in English) to accommodate localization.
rule: Keep the title within 48 English characters so translation can lengthen it.

quote: Use the first sentence of the body text to state the problem or condition in a way that is clearly relevant to the user.
rule: The body's first sentence states the problem as it matters to the reader, without repeating the title, and is left out if it adds nothing.

quote: Use the second sentence to state what the user can do to resolve the problem or revert the state.
rule: The second sentence says how to fix the problem or undo the condition, without Please.

quote: Explain how to resolve the problem or revert the state even if that explanation is obvious,
rule: Give the fix even when it seems obvious, unless it cannot be said briefly or there is nothing to do (ignored characters).

quote: Use complete sentences with ending punctuation.
rule: Body text is complete sentences in sentence case with full stops.

quote: Use no more than 200 characters (in English) to accommodate localization.
rule: Keep the body within 200 English characters so translation can lengthen it.

quote: Use the exact title text, including its capitalization.
rule: Help text cites a field message by its exact title.

quote: Refer to the component as a balloon, not as a notification or an alert.
rule: Help text calls a message pointing at a control a balloon, not a notification or alert.

quote: When possible, format the title text using bold text.
rule: Help text shows the message title in bold.

quote: There is no standard search control, but you should strive to make your program's search features consistent with those of Windows.
rule: Make the app's search behave like the system's own search on that platform.

quote: Are specific objects difficult to find?
rule: Offer search where objects are many, scattered (as in trees) or found by hidden data, or where people look for text within documents.

quote: Does your feature return relevant search results within five seconds?
rule: If search cannot return relevant results within five seconds, use a design with visible progress, such as a search window.

quote: In Instant search mode, a clear button appears after the user starts typing;
rule: Once something is typed, the search field shows a clear button; during a slow search the same button stops it.

quote: For application windows, locate Search in the upper-right corner.
rule: Place a window's search field at the top trailing corner; in popup windows wherever it fits best.

quote: If Search is usually the first thing users do in a window (the primary entry point), center it at the top of the window.
rule: When searching is the first thing people do in a window, centre the search field at the top.

quote: Use the standard search button graphics.
rule: Use the standard search symbols: magnifier alone for instant search, magnifier on a button for a search run on request, and a drop-down arrow when scope or settings can change.

quote: Don't use a label; use an optional prompt instead.
rule: A search field has no label but may carry a prompt giving its scope (Search for pictures) or Type to search.

quote: On input focus, automatically select any previously entered text.
rule: When the search field takes focus, select its previous text so typing replaces it and arrows edit it.

quote: Assign the keyboard shortcut for the Search box to be Ctrl+E.
rule: Ctrl+E moves to the search field.

quote: Support Instant search whenever possible.
rule: Search as people type wherever possible, adding search-on-request only where waiting is worth it.

quote: Regular searches must return relevant results within five seconds and Instant search must return results within two seconds.
rule: Instant search shows results within two seconds and search-on-request within five, then may keep adding less relevant results while the app stays usable.

quote: If you provide both regular and Instant search modes, the Instant search results must be a subset of the regular search results.
rule: When both kinds of search exist, instant results are a subset of the full results.

quote: All searching is prefix-based (no substring or suffix searching).
rule: Search matches the beginnings of words, treats a trailing wildcard as optional, and joins several words with OR.

quote: Multiple searches result in a single virtual page, so clicking Back always returns the original page.
rule: Search results form one page in the Back history, however many searches are made, so Back, Esc or an empty search returns to the original view.

quote: If necessary for scale, rank the search results by relevance.
rule: Rank results by relevance when there are many.

quote: A blank search returns the original page.
rule: Clearing the search field restores the original view.

quote: either make it an instruction (for example, Type to search) or indicate the scope of the search (for example, Search for pictures).
rule: The search prompt is a word or short phrase: an instruction (Type to search) or the scope (Search for pictures).

quote: Use sentence-style capitalization.
rule: The search prompt is in sentence case.

quote: Don't use ending punctuation or ellipsis.
rule: The search prompt ends without punctuation or ellipsis.

quote: Refer to this control as the Search box.
rule: Help text calls the control the Search box, capital S and lowercase box.

quote: Refer to the two types of search as Instant search and regular search.
rule: Help text says Instant search and regular search, capitalised as shown.
